answers.children: Yes — Tibetan Terriers are good with children when raised together because their medium size, affectionate nature and protective streak let them bond closely while standing guard over toddlers as they did in Tibetan monasteries. Their independent streak can appear as stubbornness around boisterous play, yet the breed’s alertness keeps them watchful rather than overwhelmed. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Tibetan Terriers usually get along with other pets thanks to their sociable yet reserved temperament and lack of strong prey drive. They form deep family bonds and tolerate household companions once introduced, though their alert watchdog heritage may spark cautious barking at new animals until trust is earned.
answers.exercise: Tibetan Terriers need 45 to 60 minutes of daily exercise such as brisk walks or yard romps to stay content. Bred as active monastery companions in the Himalayas their thick double coat makes them suited to cooler outings; without this activity they become bored and may chew household items.
answers.shedding: Yes — Tibetan Terriers shed moderately with their long double coat that features a woolly undercoat for insulation and long outer hair that tangles easily. The coat evolved to shield against Himalayan snow and wind so loose hair collects indoors and requires regular removal from furniture and clothing.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Tibetan Terrier has a long double coat that sheds lightly but still releases dander and loose underwool into the home. Its thick Himalayan-derived fur requires frequent brushing to prevent mats, especially behind the elbows and ears where the outer guard hairs tangle. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic, and the Tibetan Terrier is not among those usually suggested to allergy sufferers.
answers.training: Tibetan Terriers are not easy to train because their independent streak and stubborn nature make them resistant to commands they deem unnecessary. Originally bred as watchful companions in Tibetan monasteries they think for themselves which demands patient consistent work focused on building trust rather than forcing obedience.
answers.lifespan: Tibetan Terriers live 15 to 16 years. Their long lifespan for a dog stems from the hardy build developed over 2000 years in the isolated mountains of Tibet where the thick double coat and medium proportions supported resilience in a harsh climate.
answers.size: Adult Tibetan Terriers weigh 18 to 30 lb and stand 14 to 17 in tall. This compact sturdy build with substantial bone and balanced proportions makes them feel like a solid armful that can curl comfortably on a lap or trot steadily beside their owner without being underfoot.
answers.barking: Tibetan Terriers bark a moderate amount mainly as alert watchdogs. Their history as monastery guardians in Tibet means they give a low woof or cautious bark at strangers or unusual sounds until they decide the situation is safe reflecting their protective yet non-aggressive nature.
answers.apartment: Yes — Tibetan Terriers can live in apartments provided they receive their 45 to 60 minutes of daily exercise and mental stimulation. Their adaptable nature moderate energy and indoor settling ability suit smaller homes as long as their watchdog barking is managed and they get regular outings.
answers.first-time: No — Tibetan Terriers are not ideal for first-time owners because their stubbornness high grooming demands and independent nature require consistent patience and experience. The thick long double coat alone creates a steep learning curve in maintenance that novices often underestimate.
